Retrieval-augmented generation is a common use-case for these databases to improve domain-specific responses of large language models. Retrieval can also be combined with metadata filtering or lexical search to support hybrid workflows.

bodies.thread:
Vector embeddings are mathematical representations of data in a high-dimensional space, with dimensions ranging from a few hundred to tens of thousands.

These embeddings are computed from raw data using machine learning methods like word embeddings, deep learning networks, or feature extraction algorithms.

To search for semantically similar records, these databases typically implement approximate nearest neighbor algorithms.

Common techniques for similarity search on these high-dimensional vectors include HNSW graphs, LSH and sketching, product quantization, and inverted files.

In recent benchmarks, HNSW-based implementations have been among the best performers.

Retrieval-augmented generation is a common use-case for these systems to improve domain-specific responses of large language models.

Vector retrieval can be combined with metadata filtering or lexical search to support filtered and hybrid retrieval workflows.

Vector databases enable semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation by managing high-dimensional data embeddings.
